full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha J: This appeal is directed against the order dated 30-4-94 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Naogaon in Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1992 under Order 43 rule 1(k) of the Code of Civil Procedure rejecting the appellant's prayer for substitution of the heirs and heiresses of deceased defendant No.17 Nur Mohammad on setting aside abatement. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the appellant as plaintiff instituted a suit before the Subordinate Judge, Naogaon for declaration of title in the suit land and for a further declaration that the suit property cannot be treated as vested property by the defendants. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 214:89, defendant No.19 preferred Civil Revision No.108 of 1989 (Rangpur)/Civil Revision No.1507 of 1991 (Dhaka) before the High Court Division and this Court on hearing the parties discharged the Rule by judgment dated 27- 8-1991. In this case their Lordships found that if defendant No.17 Nur Mohammad had already died, his heirs and heiresses could be substituted on setting aside abatement. Thereafter the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 23-10-91 recorded an order of abatement of the suit against deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad. It would be mentioned in this on section that this order of abatement dated 23-10-1991 was passed in the absence of the parties. There is nothing on record to show that the aforesaid order of abatement was even shown to the learned Advocates for the contending parties. In this way the suit proceeded. Thereafter on 27-6-1997 the petitioner filed an application for substitution of the heirs and heiresses of deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad on setting aside abatement alleging inter alia that the petitioner recently learnt about the death of deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad and thereafter promptly filed the application for setting aside abatement. 

 7. At the trial the plaintiff-petitioner examined one witness and the contending defendant examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective cases. 

 9. Mr SN, Goswami the learned. Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that misreading of the judgment Civil Revision No. 108 of 1989 (Rangpur) and Civil Revision No. 1507 of 1991 (Dhaka) the learned' ordinate Judge seriously erred in law in finding that since the High Court Division had already found abatement of the suit on the death of deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad, the prayer for substitution on setting aside abatement could not be allowed, although the High Court Division never found and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge also erred in law in holding of surmises and conjectures that the petitioner had earlier knowledge about the death of deemed defendant No.17 Nur Mohammad, the application for substitution on setting aside abatement is barred by limitation and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that since there is lathes and negligence on the part of the plaintiff parties to diligently pursue his case and to file the application for setting aside abatement, the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in not taking a lenient view on the matter and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 11. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has placed before us the impugned order as well as the application for substituting 4 the heiresses of deceased defendant No.17 Nur Mohammad on setting aside abatement 4 appears that the learned Subordinate Judge with reference to the judgment passed by this Court in Civil Revision No. 1507 of 1991. (Dhaka), found that this Court already found that the suit had abated against deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad although this Court, found as in the judgment in question. Rather it appears from the judgment passed in Civil Revision No. 1507 of 1991 that their Lordships found that if at all abatement took place on account of the death of deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad, the said abatement could be set aside in due course of law. PW 1 clearly stated in his evidence that the plaintiff had no earlier knowledge about the death of deceased defendant Nur Mohammad The learned Subordinate Judge evidently passed the order bf abatement on an off date on 23-10-1991 beyond the knowledge of the petitioner. There is absolutely nothing on record to show that the order of abatement was ever shown to the learned Advocate for the petitioner or it was brought to the notice of the petitioner. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, it cannot be said that the petitioner had earlier knowledge about the death of deceased defendant No.17 Nur Mohammad and the plaintiff had any laches and negligence in praying for Substitution Of the heirs of deceased defendant Nur Mohammad on setting aside abatement. The finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that since the question of abatement was raised in Civil Revision No. 1507 of 1991, the petitioner must have earlier know ledge about the death of deceased defendant Nur Mohammad is found to be based on no concrete facts and sound reasoning`s and consequently the void finding is set aside in the interest of justice. 

 13. It has been consistently held by the superior Courts of the subcontinent that the provisions of Order 22 rule 9(2)(3) of the Code should be liberally construed. Abatement of a suit precludes a fresh suit on the same cause of action without a trial of the ease on merit. If abatement is not set aside, the applicant is deprived of the opportunity of proving his Claim only on account of his being late in praying for setting aside abatement. Ordinarily there is no reason for applicant to make a willful default, for he gets no benefit for coming late. On the other hand, if delay is condoned and substitution is allowed, a cause can be decided on merit after hearing the parties. In support of his submission Mr Goswami has placed before us the case of Azimunnessa vs Rup Gazi, reported in 39 DLR 6. in which, it has been held that unless there is gross negligence and laches on the part of the applicant, the Court should liberally, .consider the prayer for setting aside abatement as an abatement deprives, the applicant the opportunity of proving his claims.  The view taken in the cited decision applies to the facts and circumstances of the Present case. The scope of Order 22 rule 9(2)(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure has been illustrated by our Appellate Division in the case of Abdul Kader Mondal vs Md Shamsur Rahman Chowdhury in Civil Petition No. 40 of 1995. In the facts of the case and the materials on record, we are satisfied to hold that the petitioner had no earlier knowledge about the death of deceased defendant Nur Mohammad and he bonafide filed the application for substituting the heirs and heiresses of deceased defendant Nur Mohammad on setting aside abatement. The learned Subordinate Judge on an erroneous view of law and fact rejected the petitioner's application for setting aside abatement. 

 14. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, we are of the view that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the law bearing on the subject and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellant are accordingly sustained. 

 15. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost and the impugned order dated 30-4-94 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Naogaon in Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1992 rejecting the petitioner's prayer for substitution of the heirs and heiresses of deceased defendant No.17 Nur Mohammad on setting aside abatement is set aside and the petitioner's application for substitution on setting aside abatement of the death of deceased defendant No. 17 Nur Mohammad is allowed. Misc. Case No. 80 of 1992 stands allowed accordingly. 

 16. In view of the fact that this is an old case, it is necessary in the interest of justice that the suit be disposed of expeditiously. The learned Subordinate Judge, Naogaon is hereby directed to dispose of the suit as expeditiously as possible, preferably within 6 months from date of the receipt of this order.
